## Feature Summary

The plan for #655 turns each of the 21 Medium review findings into a task of the piece that owns it or records a reason it is not needed. Notes are fixed where the text is touched anyway.

## Problem Statement

Independent readers found 21 Medium findings while reviewing the issue-polling orchestrator design spec. None is fixed in the spec; the plan and pull request workers must handle them. About 40 notes remain in the source reports.

## User Story

Not known yet

## Proposed Solution

Run `/sc:workflow` on the approved spec for #655. Turn each Medium finding into a task of the piece that owns it or record a reason it is not needed. Fix notes where the text is touched anyway. The notes stay in the source reports: spec-review-part1.md, spec-review-part2.md, spec-review-part1-r2.md, and spec-review-part2-r3.md, kept in the orchestrator session records, not in this repo.

## From review 1, part 1 (spec-review-part1.md): Medium

Real defects that no named decision rests on; follow-up candidates.

- **M1. What happens to an assigned issue that is filtered out (unlisted or disabled repo, other assignee, day cap) is undefined, so R7 or the "Needs you proposal once" rule fails.** The store has no state for a skipped issue (4.10 `ENTRY_STATES`: `pending, woken, acked, unknown, failed, abandoned`), and step 8 filters before candidates exist. Either the issue stays "new" every cycle (a wake every 5 minutes, against R7 and the zero-token metric) or it is dropped silently (4.4's "Needs you proposal the orchestrator makes once when an issue shows up in an unlisted repo" has no producer, and the wake example shows `repo_not_listed` inside `skipped[]`). Evidence: spec lines 243 to 248, 290, 277, 174, 193, 390. The 17 open assigned issues found today include repos (IronOrca 5, Coder 3, Ironeye 1) that may not be listed.
- **M2. `--take` contradicts the wake rules.** Section 4.3 rule 2 (line 244) says `--take` "writes a synthetic wake"; wave 0 (line 440) says `--take` has no wake file and no acknowledgment "because the poll alone writes wake files"; 3.7 item 3 says the orchestrator never writes a wake file.
- **M3. Acknowledgment reasons are not in the poll's closed reason table.** 3.6 has the poll record skip reasons such as `claimed_elsewhere`; the acknowledgment also carries `malformed_item`, `co_assigned`, claim stops. None is among the 53 reasons of 4.7. `audit.py:280` and `:393` reject any reason not in `REASONS`, and 4.7 says a test asserts the table's exact contents, so the quoted 53 and that test are wrong if these are logged as reasons. Decide: store them as free `ack_reason` text outside the audit reasons, or add them to the table.
- **M4. `origin_mismatch` has three meanings.** Today it is a cycle reason with exit 2 (`audit.py:32`) used for the one worktree (`cycle.py:670-678`); `Config.worktree` is removed. 4.4 says a per-repo mismatch "is `origin_mismatch` and the issue is skipped"; the wake schema (3.4) lists `origin_mismatch` as a `checkout_state` of an `assigned` item (not skipped); DQ4 makes it escalation rule 8. 4.7 says every other reason keeps its kind and exit code, so a per-repo mismatch would stop the whole cycle with exit 2 unless the spec says otherwise.
- **M5. `gate-create` needs a Task and waves 0 to 3 have none.** `orca orchestration gate-create --help`: `--task <task_id>` is required. Escalations that happen before wave 4 creates a Task (malformed wake, `E-REPO-UNLISTED`, `E-CHECKOUT`, `E-CLAIM-STOP`, rule 8 on a failed worktree) still say "creates a decision gate" (5.6 item 2; template status line `Orca gate: <gate id>`). The spec does not say which Task such a gate attaches to.
- **M6. The DQ3 lease has no lifecycle for the winner.** Only the loser edits its lease to `released`. A winner that stops (`E-CLAIM-STOP`, skipped, escalated, merged and closed) keeps the lowest comment id forever, so any later orchestrator, or the same one after a reopen and `--take`, loses with `claimed_elsewhere`. "Its own lease" is also ambiguous when a host holds an old lease of a finished run. Evidence: spec line 105 (DQ3 layer 4) and wave 1 (line 448 to 451).
- **M7. ADD1 does not state how the worker brief guard passes for the `/sc:pr-submit` `Command:` line.** `WORKER-CONTRACT.md:16` and `:20` make the guard refuse the whole brief before anything runs when a `Command:` line names a never-as-worker command, and `:23` says "If D3 adds a worker route for pr-submit, D3 also states how that route passes the brief guard." The handoff (5.4 section 6) puts `/sc:pr-submit --monitor 3 --head {{branch}}` on a `Command:` line. ADD1 adds a `Flow: orchestrated-issue` line but says nothing about the guard or WC-9 override wording; the first live worker would send `guard refused:`. (`/sc:implement` also has no `## Unattended mode`, `grep -c unattended src/superclaude/commands/implement.md` is 0, so how its worker contract and report directory work in this flow is not stated either.)
- **M8. Cross-repo `worker-start` is presented as settled, but the coordinator spec records it as unproven.** `SPEC-AGENT-WORK-COORDINATOR-20261027.md` line 408 ("Cross-repo `worker-start` is unproven") and line 380. The orchestrator session runs in the orchestrator repo's workspace and wave 4 starts a worker in another repo's worktree. It is not in section 12 (U1 to U24) and not marked UNVERIFIED in wave 4.
- **M9. The plan-agent brief (wave 2) takes `<issue scope>` from issue text with no data rule.** The handoff template quotes issue text as fenced data (5.4 item 3), but the wave 2 `Command: /sc:analyze <issue scope> ...` has no such rule, and that agent runs in the user's real claim checkout (`path:<checkout>`), unbound, with no L1 or L2 guard (DQ7). Issue text is attacker-influenced (anyone with triage can assign). Say how `<issue scope>` is derived (a validated path or a fixed string) and where `<dir>` is.
- **M10. Idle hourly wakes and a never-cleared session spend tokens.** The hourly wake line (DQ10) is not gated on "a worker is in progress", so an idle hour starts a model turn that ends in `E-NO-WAKE`; neither it nor the poll's typed line clears the permanent session, while the report waker clears before every morning wake because a resumed conversation costs about 546k tokens a call (`waker.py:230-235`). 5.5 says the session "may be cleared" but names no step that does it. This works against "when nothing is new, no tokens are spent".
- **M11. The merge gate's closed `reasons` list does not map every `merge_wait` outcome.** `reviewers.py:395-424` returns `polling`, `clean`, `findings`, `declined`, `no_response`, `timeout`. The spec's closed set (line 485) has `review_pending` and `review_none_present` only; `declined` (Augment declined) and `timeout` (an active reviewer incomplete) and `findings` have no stated reason or mapping to hold, so `merge-gate` can return `merge_ok` or a reason the test list does not know.
- **M12. A restart with `worker_start_intent` and no worker found is not settled.** Wave 4 (line 472) says a found worker is adopted; it does not say what happens when `worker-list` shows none (start again, which can double-start if Orca lists late, or escalate). The existing text it builds on says the opposite of R5 here: `sc-issue-protocol/SKILL.md:140` ("with no worker the row stays for a person to settle"). R5 says retry once, so the spec must say how that retry is told apart from a start that is still in flight (for example `request-show` with a stored `--retry-request` id, which the spec only lists as UNVERIFIED U21).

## From review 1, part 2 (spec-review-part2.md): Medium

Real weaknesses that nothing named rests on. Listed as follow-up candidates.

- **M1. After C1 to C19 the coordinator spec still contradicts itself.** `/agent-coordinator` and the `.claude/skills` layout survive at lines 41 (scope), 61 (Form row: "Three skills under `.claude/skills/`: agent-work-report, agent-coordinator, agent-session-manager, following the `/prd` layout"), 64 ("one fixed coordinator workspace"), 89 and 336 (diagrams), 120 (acceptance: "follows the `/prd` layout ... under the length target"), 122 ("the coordinator folder holds the repo map template", but C4 moves the map to `orchestrator.json`), 364, 373, 424 (tests "in IronFlow"), 428 (FR-1 test row: "`/prd` layout") and 464 (M2 Coordinator). C6 says the orchestrator skill does not follow `/prd`; C18 turns the 4.1 row 323 path into `src/superclaude/skills/agent-coordinator/`, a folder that will never exist. The `diff -q` check of 6.1 passes on two equally inconsistent copies. Evidence: Grep and sed of the coordinator spec at those lines.
- **M2. WC-17 is the only contract text for the worker side of the kept G2 rule 2.** 7.2 removes WC-17 whole, but its sentence "The worker's `ask` and `send` commands carry no `--to`: Orca's default is the owning Run mailbox ... and the launch-level guard blocks any `--to` from a bound worker" (`WORKER-CONTRACT.md:59`) exists nowhere else (`--to` appears elsewhere only at line 79, an unrelated rule), and `tests/skills/test_worker_contract.py:444-445` asserts it. 7.3 keeps the guard rule and says it is "needed by any governed worker". Move that sentence into a kept section before deleting WC-17, or the kept guard rule has no contract text and its test assertion is dropped.
- **M3. Section 8.2 omits a dependency of PR B on PR C.** T9 requires `report.html` and the `orchestrated/` entry file to appear and move to `closed/`; those come from `run.py refresh` and the changed `previous_notes`, which are PR C (DQ12, wave 3: "before PR C this step is skipped and recorded as a warning"). 8.2 lists PR B as waiting for A, the nine tests and O1 only, and PR C as waiting for O1 only. State that T9 needs the PR C branch (built, not necessarily merged).
- **M4. T5 introduces a failpoint in production code with no design.** `SUPERCLAUDE_TEST_FAILPOINTS=1` "stops `superclaude orchestrator state` right after an `intent` line" (line 725). Grep finds `FAILPOINT` nowhere in `src` or `tests` today and nowhere else in the spec (not in 5.1, 5.5, the verb list of ADD6 or 9.1). A production verb that exits on an environment variable is a behaviour the file table, tests and the "no mocks or fallbacks in production code" rule must cover, or T5 should kill the process from outside.
- **M5. OD1 does not tell the owner what option A leaves open.** OD1 recommends A (workers push their own branch, run with no launch-level guard and no pre-push hook). DQ8 records that IronClaude `master` is not protected (`protected: false`, no rulesets; verified read-only today: `permissions` show push true, admin false). Together, a worker steered by issue text can push to `master` and only its written prompt stops it; K12 rates this M/H but OD1, the text the owner reads, does not say so. Add the sentence to OD1 so the choice is informed.
- **M6. No pull request carries the design doc itself.** Issue "Documentation Needs" lists "a new design doc for this orchestrator". 8.1 has PR A to E and O1 to O5; PR E only edits the status line of `orchestrator.md`, which implies the doc is already merged. The commit `427baacd5` is local on `clayphi/issue-655-spec`. Say which pull request (a docs-only one before PR D, or PR D) lands it and when.
- **M7. UNVERIFIED items without a concrete command.** U23 ("a test with a triage-only account would settle it") names no command; U19 relies on `gh issue view 444` plus "the owner reconciles"; U17 ("Read `page.py` and `render.py`") and U10 give a procedure but no command. Every other item (U1 to U9, U11 to U16, U18, U20 to U22, U24) names a runnable command or file.

## From re-review, part 1 (spec-review-part1-r2.md): Medium

- **N-M1. Nothing restarts a dead orchestrator session while workers are in flight.** The fix deletes the `coordinator-hourly` waker (DQ10, C17, O3 and O4). That hourly wake was the only trigger that started a missing session without a new assignment (`waker.py:214-217`, `start_session`). Now the poll starts a session only when it has a wake to send (4.5 step 11), and DQ10 says "with no worker in flight there is nothing to check". If the orchestrator session ends or Claude Code dies with workers running, their `ask`, `worker_done` and the pull request watch go unread until the next new assignment. Wave 0's `--resume` defines what a start does, not what causes one. Suggest: the poll also wakes (mailbox plus typed line, or starts the session) when any `.orchestrator/issues/*.json` is `in_progress` and no live orchestrator session exists, or `orchestrator-poll` marks the workspace unread in that case.
- **N-M2. 4.3 rule 2 and 4.5 step 8 omit `failed` entries.** Step 8 filters S1 by "no store entry (4.3)" and rule 2 (changed line 244) now lists what happens to `acked`, `pending`, `woken`, `unknown` and `abandoned` entries, but not `failed`. A pre-pending failure (for example a transient re-read error) leaves a `failed` entry; as written that issue is never a candidate again, so the retry that leads to `attempts_exhausted` (exit 7, the PR A test row, 3.7 item 1 "or 3 failed preparations") is unreachable and the old silent drop remains for this path. 4.10 keeps `fail`, `backoff_elapsed`, `BACKOFF` and the `in_backoff` reason, so the intent is clear; the two text lines need to say `failed` entries are re-examined once their backoff has elapsed. Evidence: old behaviour `cycle.py:934-935` (`backoff_elapsed` then `in_backoff`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The plan for #655 turns each Medium finding into a task of the piece that owns it or records a reason it is not needed.
- [ ] Notes are fixed where the text is touched anyway.

## Out of Scope

Not known yet

## Components Affected (from `/sc:analyze`)

The findings name the poll script, orchestrator skill, skill move, retirement of the old approval code, fixtures and runbook. The spec under review is `docs/designs/orchestrator.md` on branch `clayphi/issue-655-spec`, not merged. No codebase pass was performed.

## Related Issues/PRs

- #655: parent issue. Its design spec on branch `clayphi/issue-655-spec` is not merged.
- #651: plan format, dependency of #655.

## Findings from the review of PR 681 (spec landing)

PR 681 lands the owner-approved design `docs/designs/orchestrator.md` unchanged. The Augment and Codex reviews raised six findings about its text. The owner approved the text byte for byte, so none was fixed in that docs-only pull request. They are recorded here for the follow-up of the design.

1. [Codex P2, line 565](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/pull/681#discussion_r4636029171): the wave 4 worktree helper takes its source checkout from the current directory, so it must be run from the issue's repo checkout and not from the orchestrator repo.
2. [Codex P2, line 708](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/pull/681#discussion_r4636029179): a `done` or `skipped` issue that is reopened or reassigned cannot be retaken, because `--take` creates the state file exclusively and only three `escalated` endings are archived.
3. [Augment high, line 350](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/pull/681#discussion_r4636047200): the sample poll precheck runs `superclaude issue-watch once` without `--dry-run`, while the shadow phase is meant to be a dry run (section 4.8 adds the flag), so the sample can be mistaken for the shadow command.
4. [Augment medium, line 300](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/pull/681#discussion_r4636047209): the validator accepts `max_in_flight` from 1 to 10, while goal G5 and owner ruling 8 say at most 3 issues in flight per orchestrator.
5. [Augment medium, line 480](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/pull/681#discussion_r4636047217): wave 0 does not cancel a plan request when the live issue no longer carries `hold:plan`, so a label removed by hand after dispatch can still start `/sc:issue --plan`.
6. [Augment medium, line 702](https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/pull/681#discussion_r4636047226): a plan request acknowledged as skipped for `held_backlog` has no plan record, so the in-flight count treats it as in flight and a lasting backlog label can hold a slot and trigger extra orchestrators.

## Follow-ups from the review of PR 684 (the report skill moved into IronClaude)

These findings are about code moved unchanged from the IronFlow repository (or were left out of PR 684 on purpose). None was fixed in that pull request.

1. **Local report server (security).** `page.py` `ensure_server` runs `python -m http.server --directory .dev/coordinator` on 127.0.0.1:8765. It serves the whole state folder with a directory listing and accepts any Host header, so a page in the operator's browser that uses DNS rebinding could read run files and transcript excerpts. Fix: serve only `report.html`, reject any Host other than 127.0.0.1:8765, and turn the listing off.
2. **Item titles are not quoted as data.** An instruction-shaped title (a renamed issue or task) reaches the report session as raw Markdown. Fix: quote the title on its own line; this changes the item template, the heading rule in `check.py` and the parsing in `page.py`.
3. **A ClickUp task whose only GitHub link is in a comment loses that link** once the comment leaves the collection window, so the task gets its own card again.
4. **Replies inside a ClickUp comment thread** are collected but not printed in `activity.md`, so the report session never sees a reply that asks the owner something.
5. **Removed in PR 684 because the spec does not ask for it:** the carry-forward of ClickUp tasks and sessions across a claim (each review round found a deeper case in it). If the owner wants it back it needs its own design.

**Release blocker (security):** item 1 of the comment above (the local report server serves the whole state folder and accepts any Host header) is a security item that MUST be fixed before the next IronClaude release. Raised by the owner's channel after PR 684 merged (squash d7d645ddd). Items 2 to 5 are ordinary follow-ups.

## Findings from the review of PR 686 (PR A, the poll core): required before the poll is switched on

PR 686 ships the poll with `enabled: false`. Codex raised these seven findings; none is a bug that blocks merging disabled code, but each must be resolved before switch-on (the shadow run will also show whether they matter).

1. `cycle.py` `_ack_step`: an acknowledgment of the first wake is not read after a resend replaces the entry's `wake_id` (one `wake_id` per entry in the schema-2 store); the entry can end abandoned although the orchestrator took the wake. Fix: read acknowledgments of earlier unarchived wake files, or change the schema.
2. `github.py` org-wide search bound (100 rows) counts unlisted repos, so someone who can assign the account in an unlisted repo could stop the poll (availability). Fix: query listed repos only (changes discovery and the call budget).
3. `github.py` timeline read is one page of 100: the newest events of a long issue can be missed. Fix: bounded pagination (a new allowed argv form).
4. `cycle.py` day-cap reservations of plan requests that routing then declines can crowd out a ready assignment in the same cycle (cycle order).
5. `cycle.py` a failing resume of a dead orchestrator keeps no attempt count and retries every cycle (restart state in the store or registry).
6. `cycle.py` `last_poll_at` advances although information items beyond the 50-item limit (or a failed information-only delivery) were not delivered (needs a cursor that cannot pass undelivered items).
7. (fixed in the PR) registry probes fell back to a 1 s call with no allowance.

## Closing: not planned: the parent design was retired (backlog review, 2026-11-24)

Closed on the owner's instruction after an independent review passed.

- Parent #655 was closed as not planned on the owner's 2026-11-23 decision: merged PR #707 is the design, the archived branches are kept, and uncovered features are tracked in #716, #717 and #718 (https://github.com/IronbellyOrg/IronClaude/issues/655#issuecomment-7089440080).
- PR #700 rolled back the #655 design and report skill, so the plan this issue wanted findings handled in no longer exists.
- No claim is made that the 21 findings are fixed.

_Limits: the full GitHub event timeline could not be read in this review and is unverified. Reopen if the evidence above is wrong._

title: [FEATURE] Handle the 21 Medium review findings in the plan for #655
